title: Hidden and long-term unemployment
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:33Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest points cover measuring unemployment and its causes and effects, but none teaches hidden or long-term unemployment specifically, so this needs a new point.

draft.title: Hidden and long-term unemployment
card: People who want a job but have stopped looking, often because they think none is available. They are not in the official unemployment rate, so it can understate how many people lack work.
Being out of work for a year or more. It is a serious problem because the person's skills can fall out of date, and employers may be less willing to hire them.
The two ideas are different. Hidden unemployment is about not being counted, because the person is no longer looking. Long-term unemployment is about how long a person has been out of work.
Both can be higher when jobs are hard to find. Long-term unemployment also makes it harder for a person to return to work, because skills and contacts fade.
draft.remember: Hidden unemployment is wanting work but not looking. Long-term unemployment is a year or more out of work.

a.q: Which person is part of hidden unemployment?
opts: Sam wants a job but stopped searching after many rejections
Priya has been looking for work for the past 14 months
Tom works two days a week and wants more shifts
Lena has left her job and starts a new one next week
a.why: Sam wants work but has stopped looking, so he is not counted as unemployed. Priya is long-term unemployed, but she is still looking, so she is in the official figures.
a.clue: Hidden means not looking, so not counted.

b.q: Daniel lost his factory job in Wollongong 18 months ago and is still applying for jobs each week. How is he best described?
opts: Long-term unemployed, and counted in the official rate
Hidden unemployed, and left out of the official rate
Long-term unemployed, and left out of the official rate
Hidden unemployed, and counted in the official rate
b.why: Daniel has been out of work for over a year, so he is long-term unemployed. He is still looking for work, so he is counted in the official rate. Hidden unemployment applies only to people who have stopped looking.
b.clue: Check how long he has been out of work, and whether he is still searching.

a.best: Sam wants a job but stopped searching after many rejections

b.best: Long-term unemployed, and counted in the official rate
